events.title: St. Bernard preaches the Second Crusade at Vézelay
events.shortBlurb: At the pope's bidding, the abbot of Clairvaux roused France to a new crusade, and the king of France took the cross…
body: On 31 March 1146, at the Easter assembly on the hillside of Vézelay in Burgundy, Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, preached the Second Crusade before King Louis VII of France, Queen Eleanor, and a great gathering of nobles. Pope Eugene III, once Bernard's own monk, had charged him with the task after Zengi, atabeg of Mosul, took Edessa on 24 December 1144, destroying the first of the crusader states.

The response overwhelmed the supply of cloth crosses, and Bernard is said to have cut up his own habit to make more; the king and his barons knelt to receive the cross. Bernard then carried the preaching into Germany, where he won King Conrad III at Speyer and silenced the monk Rudolf, whose agitation had stirred massacres of Jews in the Rhineland.

The crusade of 1147 to 1149 ended in failure before Damascus, a humiliation Bernard answered in his apology to the pope, set down in the second book of 'De consideratione', where he laid the disaster upon the sins of the crusaders themselves. Edessa was never recovered.
